bib.title: Further Topics (Chapter 4 of Multimodal Deep Learning)
bib.venue: book chapter, Multimodal Deep Learning (Akkus et al.)

question: How do multimodal models extend beyond text and images: further modalities, tabular plus unstructured data, multipurpose multitask models, and generative art?
contributions: A challenge-based taxonomy of multimodal learning (representation, alignment, fusion, translation)
Overview of general architectures (NUWA, Perceiver IO, HiP) and training paradigms (data2vec, VATT, MultiMAE)
Survey of structured plus unstructured data fusion, mostly survival analysis and economics
Comparison of multipurpose models (MultiModel, UniT, OFA, Gato) and Pathways-related work (PathNet, LIMoE, muNet)
Overview of generative art with CLIP-guided models

limits: Almost no experimental numbers: model comparisons are qualitative and the one comparison table has blank or ambiguous cells (OFA row).
4.1.2.2.3 describes the authors' own unpublished non-contrastive latent-prediction research with no results.
Chapter authors concede multipurpose models lack suitable metrics and are hard to compare (curse of dimensionality).
Structured+unstructured studies often skip single-modality baselines; hyperparameter and modality-combination search, small samples and publication bias may inflate results.
Dated 2022: DALL-E 2 named as newest; Gato, OFA, Pathways, GLIDE are pre-2023 state of art.
Many citations are unresolved ('(?)', garbled bib keys) so some claims lack a traceable source.
practices: Choose fusion by depth: early (merge at input), joint (merge learned latents, end-to-end), late (merge predictions) (4.2.3).
Prefer end-to-end learning over separate feature extraction followed by a model (4.2.5).
Benchmark multimodal models against single-modality baselines, especially structured-only (4.2.5).
Avoid feature overlap between linear and NN parts of Wide & Deep, or orthogonalize (two-stage or in-model) to keep identifiability (4.2.4.3, 4.2.4.4).
Use multimodal dropout (drop whole modalities in training) to cope with missing modalities at inference (4.2.4.3).
Use latent-prediction SSL to avoid hard-negative mining and data-space decoders (4.1.2.2.1).
Mask consecutive chunks, not single rows, for long correlated inputs (4.1.2.2.3).
For MoE multimodal models, add local and global entropy losses to balance routing across modalities (4.3.3.3).

terms.definition: projecting a concatenated multimodal input into one representation space
learn different representation spaces for each modality and coordinate them such that we can sensibly align these representation spaces and apply a common distance function
merge at input layer / merge learned latents inside the model with backprop / fuse predictions of per-modality models
drops entire modalities during training in order to make models less dependent on one single data source
generator (artist) plus a critic such as CLIP that scores whether output matches the text
